items.title: Dan Morgenstern — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The incumbent band for a very long time was Red Allen... and for a while, Cozy Cole on drums.

ctx.x: We were going to pick up with your enrolling in Brandeis without your knowledge.

I came in the middle of the academic year. I had gotten out of the Army in January. So right after the winter break I arrived at Brandeis. It was very small then. The first class had just graduated. That was the class of 1952. They had just graduated the previous fall. It was still very small, about 700 undergraduate students, and a great faculty. I quickly made some friends. I was older. I’m 24 now, right? Yes, I’m 24. Of course that was a little more than the average age certainly of incoming freshmen, but…

There was no jazz instruction at Brandeis, needless to say. It had a very good music department, with an all-star faculty of Harold Shapiro and the very gifted, excellent composer, who died very young, named Irving Fine. The titular was Leonard Bernstein, who came in once a week. He was known as the airborne professor, because he flew in from New York to give a lecture which was attended by practically everybody, because he was a brilliant lecturer. items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...there's in, I'm looking right now at an article that Dan Morgenstern did on you for Downbeat...

ctx.x: "Oh no, Eddie don't do that." "Aw, don't talk back to me, you know, kidding. Oh boy. Those were good old days, boy we used to have more fun.

Just to cover one or two more odds and ends, there's in, I'm looking right now at an article that Dan Morgenstern did on you for Downbeat in the March 20, 1969 issue, it was a very nice article, and he mentioned that you had done another record with four drummers for Choral with Bobby Rosengarden, Specs Powell and Jimmy Crawford. That's before the one that you did with Krupa and Ray McKinley.

And Panama, that's right. We had all different rhythms on this other one that I did. Well one of them was that "Big Noise from Winnetka." See, and all I wanted Specs Powell to just play the tympany, Jimmy Crawford just to play that cymbal. Bobby Rosengarden to play the 6-8 time, and me I'd just weave in between all of them.
